question: Which of the chemical formulae represents bleaching powder?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ca(ClO)_2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bleaching Powder**, also known as **Calcium Hypochlorite (Ca(ClO)_2)**, is a widely used chemical compound for bleaching and disinfecting purposes. It is classified as a chlorinated lime compound.
 
• Bleaching powder is produced by reacting **calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)_2)** with chlorine gas (Cl_2). The chemical reaction leads to the formation of calcium hypochlorite, which is the active ingredient in bleaching powder.
 
• Its primary function is as a **disinfectant** in water treatment processes, helping to kill bacteria, viruses, and other microorganisms. It is also used in sanitizing swimming pools.
 
• Bleaching powder is used in the textile industry for bleaching cotton and linen fabrics, as well as in paper manufacturing for the bleaching of wood pulp.
 
• The formula **Ca(ClO)_2** denotes the composition of bleaching powder, which includes calcium, oxygen, and chlorine atoms essential for its bleaching and disinfecting properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uses of Bleaching Powder:**

 
 
• It is extensively used in households and industries for **disinfection** of drinking water to make it safe for consumption.
 
• In agriculture, it is used to **purify irrigation water**, ensuring plant health and controlling waterborne diseases.
 
• Bleaching powder is used in hospitals and public places for **sanitization** purposes and as an effective disinfectant.
 
• It finds applications in **swimming pool maintenance** to control microbial growth and maintain hygiene standards.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Properties:**
 
 
• Bleaching powder is a **white or light yellowish powder**, with a strong chlorine smell.
 
• It releases chlorine gas when it reacts with acids, enhancing its bleaching and disinfecting ability.
 
• It is **soluble in water**, forming a solution that is used for bleaching and disinfecting purposes.
 
• Over time, bleaching powder loses its effectiveness due to exposure to air and moisture, releasing chlorine gas.
 
 
 
• **Safety Precautions:**
 
 
• Bleaching powder should be stored in a **cool and dry place** to prevent decomposition and chlorine loss.
 
• Direct contact with skin or eyes must be avoided as it can cause **irritation or burns**.
 
• Its use in water treatment should follow **controlled dosages** to avoid overchlorination, which can harm aquatic life.
 
 
 
• **Other Chemical Formulas Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Ca(ClO_2)_2**: Represents calcium chlorite, which is not related to bleaching powder. It is incorrect.
 
• **Ca(ClO_2)**: This formula does not represent any widely used compound and is chemically incorrect.
 
• **Ca_2(ClO)_2**: This formula is incorrect and does not represent bleaching powder.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** Bleaching powder was first discovered in the 18th century by Scottish chemist **Charles Tennant** as a bleaching agent for the textile industry.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** Excessive use of bleaching powder in water can lead to **chlorine contamination**, which may affect aquatic ecosystems.
 
• **Regulation:** In India, the use of bleaching powder for drinking water treatment is regulated under **guidelines issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)**.
 
• **Global Usage:** It is a widely used chemical compound in various industries across **developed and developing countries**, including India, the USA, and China.
